rules.source: crates.io's default max_upload_size of 10 MiB per .crate; no Bifrost crate has a raised limit. v0.14.3's largest, brokk-bifrost-store, was 3251619 bytes.
PyPI's default per-file limit of 100 MiB. v0.14.2's manylinux aarch64 wheel (104698118 bytes) uploaded; v0.14.3's was refused with 400 File too large (release run 40897040195).

PyPI's default per-file limit of 100 MiB; the project has no raised limit. The raw binary deflated to 97.7 MB in v0.14.3, so since #8288 the wheel carries it xz-compressed (the v0.14.3 manylinux x86_64 binary rewrites to a 54656836-byte wheel) and its launcher unpacks it on first run.

npm publishes no exact tarball limit. @brokkai/bifrost-darwin-universal@0.14.2 (199943577 bytes) published; 0.14.3 (205.5 MB) was refused with 413 Payload Too Large (release run 40897040195). This is the largest size known to pass, rounded up to 200 MB. Since #8288 macOS ships one package per CPU, @brokkai/bifrost-darwin-arm64 and @brokkai/bifrost-darwin-x64, about half the universal size each.
GitHub's 2 GiB limit per release asset.
